introduction.zh: 这份内在童年性格测试把“内在小孩”作为成人当下童心的比喻，关注你现在更想怎样参与手作、画画、故事与游戏。18道原创四选一题比较好奇发问、自主试手、准备入场、生动表达、安静想象和友善同玩六种玩法。完成后查看全部原始计数和每一个最高并列，阅读各自的具体例子、相近玩法比较与可选尝试。题目不要求回忆童年，也不从现在的选择推断过去发生过什么。
introduction.en: This Inner Child Personality Test uses inner child as a metaphor for an adult’s present-day playful interests: how you would like to join crafts, drawing, stories and games now. Eighteen original four-option choices compare Curious Explorer, Independent Maker, Prepared Player, Expressive Player, Quiet Imaginer and Welcoming Companion. View all raw counts and every highest tie, with concrete examples, comparisons and optional activities. No childhood recall is requested, and present choices are not used to reconstruct past events.

instructions.zh: 按你目前更想尝试的玩法，每题选择一项。多个选项都喜欢时，选此刻更想先做的；没有特别喜欢的，选相对愿意尝试的即可，不按小时候的自己或理想形象作答。18题全部完成后显示计数与所有最高并列。可以随时退出，未完成不生成个人结果，六份公开指南仍可直接阅读。开始按钮直接进入题目，无需额外同意。
instructions.en: Choose the approach you would most like to try now. If several appeal, pick what you would do first; if none especially appeals, choose the one you are relatively willing to try. Do not answer as your childhood self or an ideal image. All eighteen choices are needed for counts and every highest tie. You may leave at any time; incomplete attempts produce no personal result, while all six public guides remain readable. Start opens questions directly without another agreement.

scoreReading.zh: 18题各选一项，对应标签加1，原始次数合计18。每题提供六种玩法中的四种；六类各出现12次，在四个位置各3次，未出现的两类不记为被拒绝。分母12是选项出现次数，不是你有多少童心、性格百分比或人群排名。所有最高计数保留完整说明；全选同一位置会六类各3，六份全部呈现，不把名单第一位当主型。差一次只是一项选择，不证明显著差异、稀有度或固定主副型，近分也不补造混合类型。计数是相对分布，一项多选必然挤掉当题其他选项，不是六项独立能力或心理特质的强度。换时间、材料、场地或同伴可能改变回答。
scoreReading.en: Choose one option in each of 18 questions; each adds one count and the total is 18. Each question offers four of six approaches. Every approach appears twelve times and three times in each position; absent approaches are not counted as rejected. Twelve is an exposure denominator, not an amount of childlike spirit, personality percentage or population rank. Every highest count retains its full guide. Choosing the same position throughout gives three each and displays all six without prioritising the first. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference, rarity or fixed primary and secondary type; close counts create no invented hybrid. Counts are relative: selecting an option displaces others in that question rather than measuring six independent abilities or psychological intensities. Time, materials, setting and company can change responses.

title.zh: 好奇发问结果：内在童年测试完整说明
title.en: Curious Explorer: Inner Child Test Full Result Guide

description.zh: 本次较常选观察材料、寻找细节与追问原因的玩法。它记录你在本题组的选择，不还原童年的你。
description.en: Read Curious Explorer through everyday questions, materials and examples. Compare five approaches without reconstructing childhood or measuring intelligence.

title.en: Where curiosity points

paragraphs.zh: 这里的好奇发问，是愿意让一件普通东西多停留片刻：纸为什么折成这个形状，水滴怎样改变颜色，一个小摆件以前怎样使用。吸引你的可能是发现过程，而非立刻完成好看的成品。结果没有证明你天生好奇、比别人聪明或小时候受过怎样的教育；同一人换一种材料也可能完全不想研究。把标签读成对本次偏好的一句提问：哪些细节值得我自愿再看一眼？
paragraphs.en: Curious Explorer concerns staying with something ordinary long enough to ask another question: why paper folds into a shape, how water changes colour or how an old object was used. Discovery may appeal more than producing an impressive finished object. The result establishes no inborn curiosity, intelligence advantage or childhood education. The same person may feel no interest in different materials. Read the label as a question about these choices: which details would I willingly give another look?

title.en: Two ways to approach a sheet of paper

paragraphs.zh: 设想你在手作角选择比较纸张，而不是照着套件完成模型。你可能先折薄纸，再折厚纸，记下折痕的差别；即使没有成品，也觉得这十分钟有意思。这是一个具体偏好的例子，不表示制作能力更强。朋友想把模型完成，同样合理。如果你下一次更喜欢独自拼装，就把新选择也留下，不用为了保持结果一致而放弃它。
paragraphs.en: Imagine choosing to compare papers at a craft corner instead of completing a model kit. You might fold a thin sheet and then a thick one, noticing how the creases differ, and enjoy ten minutes without a finished object. That illustrates a preference rather than superior making ability. A friend who wants to finish the model has an equally reasonable aim. If you prefer independent building next time, retain that choice too instead of rejecting it to remain consistent with this result.

title.zh: 在有限时间里保留发现
title.en: Keeping discovery within available time

paragraphs.zh: 日常的童心不必靠旅行或购买材料才能出现。一段下雨的窗景、图书馆的插图、一件暂时不用的小物，都可以成为注意的对象。时间、费用和场地决定这次是否方便；没有精力探索也不等于失去童心。若与别人同玩，可以先说明自己想研究哪一点，再约定是否一起看以及看多久。发现不需要把他人拖进一场没有终点的讲解。
paragraphs.en: Childlike interest need not require travel or buying materials. Rain on a window, a library illustration or a small unused object can give attention somewhere to go. Time, cost and space determine whether that fits today; lacking energy for exploration does not mean losing a childlike side. With a companion, say what you want to investigate and agree whether to look together and for how long. Discovery does not require drawing someone else into an explanation with no agreed endpoint.

title.en: Putting the interest into words

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“我想先看看两种纸的折痕，十分钟后再决定做不做模型”，而不是“我是好奇型，所以讨厌按步骤”。前一句给出对象、时间与选择余地，后一句却把标签变成限制。如果你想分享发现，先问对方有没有兴趣；对方没有兴趣不否定你的乐趣。你也不必把观察写成计划或成果，保留一个仅自己知道的小问题就足够。
paragraphs.en: You could say, “I want to compare these paper creases for ten minutes before deciding whether to make a model,” rather than making a type label a rule against instructions. The concrete sentence states an object, a time and room to change your mind. Before sharing a discovery, ask whether the other person is interested. Their lack of interest need not cancel your enjoyment. You also need not turn observations into a project or achievement; a small private question can be enough.

title.en: Comparing all five alternatives

paragraphs.zh: 自主试手重在按自己的方法动手，好奇发问重在想知道发生了什么；准备入场先弄清安排，好奇可以在清楚规则后继续追问。生动表达关心声音、动作或色彩的呈现，安静想象关心私下形成的小世界；两者都能与观察并存。友善同玩强调共同选择怎样参与，而不是一定研究同一个问题。最高并列只保留这些不同取向，不能推导“互补人格”或谁需要谁。
paragraphs.en: Independent Maker emphasises trying your own method, whereas Curious Explorer emphasises what is happening and why. Prepared Player clarifies arrangements, after which curiosity can continue. Expressive Player concerns sound, movement or colour; Quiet Imaginer concerns a privately developed world. Either can accompany observation. Welcoming Companion emphasises choosing how to participate together rather than investigating the same question. Highest ties retain these distinctions without proving complementary personalities or who needs whom.

title.en: Counterexamples remain useful

paragraphs.zh: 如果你只在熟悉材料上愿意发问，对其他活动更想按说明完成，这不构成矛盾。也可能只是这十八题提供的观察选项比较合口味，其他未提供的玩法才最吸引你。做事认真、相信科学或喜欢学习，也不能反向证明这一结果；题目没有测这些能力与态度。反例提醒你缩小描述范围，不能被解释成你压抑了自己或尚未发现真实的童年人格。
paragraphs.en: If you ask questions only about familiar materials and prefer instructions elsewhere, there is no contradiction to resolve. These eighteen questions may simply offer observation options you like, while an omitted activity would appeal most. Conscientious work, interest in science or enjoyment of learning cannot independently prove this result; those abilities and attitudes were not assessed. Counterexamples narrow the description rather than showing that you suppressed yourself or failed to discover a true childhood personality.

title.en: An optional small observation

paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，在下一次轻松活动后只记一句“我注意了什么，想不想再看一次”。可以不记录、不比较，也不必寻找童年原因。若与今天的答案不同，就把差异归还给那次情境。这个回顾没有改善、疗愈或提升好奇的承诺；目标只是让你更容易决定下一次想如何玩。公开说明可以单独阅读，分享只需公开链接，无需把自己的计数或私人回忆交出去。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, after another relaxed activity note one sentence about what caught your attention and whether you want another look. You may skip recording or comparing, and need not search for a childhood cause. If it differs from today’s answers, let that difference belong to the situation. This observation promises no improvement, healing or increase in curiosity. It simply offers language for deciding how you want to play next. Read the guide independently or share its public link without personal counts or memories.

title.en: Preparation that clarifies the activity

paragraphs.zh: 准备入场关注活动怎样进行：哪些材料可用、轮到谁、怎么结束、能不能退出。信息清楚以后，你可能很乐意加入，也可能决定不参加。结果并没有测出谨慎程度或风险判断是否准确，更不能把观察一会儿解释成童年必须保护自己。十八题中的这些选项只是给准备过程一个位置；快开始与慢开始都不是成熟、勇气或健康的评分。
paragraphs.en: Prepared Player concerns how an activity works: available materials, turns, endings and whether you may leave. Clear information may make joining appealing, or help you decide to decline. The result measures neither general caution nor accuracy in judging risks, and watching first cannot establish that you had to protect yourself as a child. These options simply give preparation a place in the set. Beginning quickly or slowly provides no maturity, courage or health score.

title.en: Watching one round of a game

paragraphs.zh: 朋友介绍新桌游时，你想先看一次示范，弄清一轮到哪里结束，然后再选要不要玩。别人边玩边学也合理，只是入场过程不同。看完示范仍不想参加，不表示准备失败；也许今天没有兴趣或时间。这个例子没有衡量你学得快不快、害不害怕。把要求说成“一轮示范”这样有界的信息，比把自己定义为永远只能准备不能行动更准确。
paragraphs.en: When a friend introduces a board game, you may prefer one demonstration to see where a round ends before deciding whether to play. Learning while playing is equally reasonable; the entry process differs. Declining after the demonstration is not failed preparation, since time or interest may be missing today. This example measures neither learning speed nor fear. Naming a bounded request such as one demonstration is more precise than defining yourself as someone who can only prepare and never act.

title.en: Arrangements depend on circumstances

paragraphs.zh: 在图书馆、公共画区或共用工具的场合，了解使用范围常常只是实际需要。活动主持有没有说清楚，也会影响你选哪项。你可以要求一张说明、一个样例或清楚的结束时间，不需要先给自己贴任何性格标签。规则清楚仍不是安全保证；现实中的风险应依据实际环境与专业要求判断，不能由这份趣味计数代替。这里的活动都以自愿、低风险和可退出为前提。
paragraphs.en: In libraries, public drawing areas or shared-tool settings, checking the scope of use can be a practical need. How clearly a host explains arrangements also affects a choice. You may ask for instructions, an example or a clear ending without assigning yourself a personality. Clear rules are not a guarantee of safety; real risks require information about the environment and relevant professional requirements rather than this playful count. Activities here assume voluntary, low-stakes participation with an available exit.

title.en: Asking for a specific piece of information

paragraphs.zh: 你可以说“我想先知道这一轮多久，是否可以只看不玩”，而不是“我就是不敢”。前一句让别人知道怎样提供信息，也保留你的决定权。对方可以回答或说明自己也不清楚，你仍可选择退出。你不必为了显得合群跳过需要的说明，也不用把偏好规则当作要求别人必须按你的方式玩；共同活动的安排需要彼此同意。
paragraphs.en: You could ask how long a round lasts and whether watching without playing is possible, instead of treating hesitation as proof that you lack courage. A specific question tells others what information would help while preserving your decision. They may answer or say they do not know, and you may still leave. You need neither skip explanations to appear sociable nor require everyone to follow your preferred process. Shared arrangements need agreement rather than a label granting authority.

title.zh: 与观察和想象分别阅读
title.en: Separating preparation, observation and imagination

paragraphs.zh: 好奇发问想研究一个现象为何如此，准备入场主要想了解参与条件；安静想象则可能在明确规则后独自进入虚构场景。自主试手偏向试自己的版本，生动表达偏向声音、动作或色彩，二者也能先准备再开始。友善同玩关注各自如何自愿加入，可能一起商量规则。不要把这六种读法排成从勇敢到害怕的序列；它们在本题里只是不同玩法选项。

Independent Maker tries a personal version, and Expressive Player favours sound, movement or colour; either may prepare first. Welcoming Companion concerns how everyone voluntarily joins and may include discussing rules. These six readings do not form a brave-to-fearful sequence. They are different approaches offered within this set.

title.zh: 直接加入不是反证失败
title.en: Joining immediately need not disprove anything

paragraphs.zh: 遇到熟悉的桌游，你也许马上加入；工具换了、场地不同，又想先了解。这说明具体条件有用，不表示前后不一致。安静的人可能迅速加入，热闹的人也会认真看规则，因此不能把本结果换算成内外向。它更不能筛查焦虑或推断神经类型。若只有某几题贴切，就把范围留在那几题，不必把每次等待都写成一种固定的童年模式。
paragraphs.en: You may immediately join a familiar game yet want information when tools or settings change. That shows the usefulness of conditions rather than inconsistency. A quiet person may join quickly and an expressive person may read instructions carefully, so this cannot convert into introversion or extraversion. It also screens for no anxiety or neurotype. If only a few choices fit, keep the description there rather than turning every pause into a fixed pattern originating in childhood.

title.zh: 留下一个可回答的问题

paragraphs.zh: 下次若遇到自愿的小活动，可以只问自己“我还缺哪一项实际信息？”它可能是步骤、时长或可不可以旁观，也可能已经没有缺口。要不要参加仍由你决定，没有必须跨出舒适区的任务。活动后可以不作记录，或记下哪条说明真正有帮助。这个回顾不提供治疗、克服恐惧或提升决策的承诺，只是把“想先准备”细化为容易表达的需要。
paragraphs.en: For another optional activity, ask which practical piece of information is still missing. It might concern steps, duration or whether watching is welcome, or there may be nothing missing. Joining remains your choice, with no assignment to leave a comfort zone. Afterwards, skip recording or note which explanation helped. This offers no treatment, fear reduction or decision-skill promise. title.zh: 私下想象也是一种玩法
title.en: Private imagining as a way to play

paragraphs.zh: 安静想象把注意放在自己慢慢形成的小世界：纸船会停在哪个港口，杯子住在怎样的房间，书架一角能装下什么场景。它不要求文学能力、长时间专注或喜欢独处，也不意味着你比别人内心丰富。你可以和朋友共享其中一部分，或完全不讲。题目只记录你更愿意选这种过程，没有测量社交需要、安静背后的原因或童年时是否常常一个人。
paragraphs.en: Quiet Imaginer places attention on a little world taking shape: a harbour for a paper boat, a room where a mug might live or a scene in a bookshelf corner. It requires no literary ability, sustained attention or general preference for solitude and establishes no richer inner life. You may share part with a friend or say nothing about it. These choices record an appealing process without measuring social needs, reasons for quietness or how often you were alone as a child.

title.en: A miniature room for a mug

paragraphs.zh: 面对一张空白纸，你可能画一个只容得下一只杯子的房间，再补一扇圆窗。没有完整故事、漂亮成品或分享对象也可以结束。朋友选择用杯子讲独白，你选择画房间，差别在玩法的焦点，不是表达深浅。你若后来想邀请朋友添一件家具，也完全相容；从私下想象转到共同创作，不会使之前的选择无效。
paragraphs.en: With a blank page, you might draw a room just large enough for a mug and add a round window. You can stop without a full story, polished result or audience. A friend giving the mug a monologue chooses a different focus, not a shallower expression. If you later invite a friend to add furniture, that fits too. Moving from private imagining to shared creation does not invalidate the earlier choice.

title.en: Quiet depends on available conditions

paragraphs.zh: 想象空间可以是一页纸、一小块桌面或几分钟空闲，并不需要长期独处。噪音、疲劳、材料与隐私都会影响这次是否想这样玩。你可以选择只有自己看的版本，也可以决定和谁分享。结果不建议减少社交，也不把不参加某次活动解释成退出关系。现实里你需要怎样的陪伴和支持，应根据自己的具体感受与关系来谈，这份趣味计数没有评估它们。
paragraphs.en: A page, a small surface or a few spare minutes can provide imagining space without prolonged solitude. Noise, fatigue, materials and privacy affect whether it appeals today. You may choose a version only you see or decide whom to share it with. The result recommends no reduction in social contact and treats declining an activity as no evidence of leaving relationships. Discuss desired company and support from your actual circumstances; these playful counts have not assessed them.

title.zh: 说明空间而不解释人格
title.en: Naming the space rather than explaining a personality

paragraphs.zh: “我想安静画十分钟，之后再决定要不要一起做”比“我属于安静型，不能和人玩”给人更多实际信息。你可以提出时长、是否欢迎旁观、哪些部分不分享，也可以改主意。别人想加入时，说明自己的安排即可，不必把他们理解成打断你的内在世界。标签没有让你必须保密或独处，它只提供一句可选的描述。
paragraphs.en: “I want ten quiet minutes to draw before deciding whether to make something together” gives more useful information than a type-based rule against playing with others. State a duration, whether watching is welcome and what remains private, and change your mind if needed. If someone asks to join, explain the arrangement without assuming an attack on an inner world. The label requires neither secrecy nor solitude; it offers an optional description.

title.zh: 与安静观察和共同创作区分
title.en: Distinguishing quiet observation and shared creation

paragraphs.zh: 好奇发问也可能安静，但主要追问现实材料；安静想象则让虚构场景慢慢出现。准备入场也可能先看，却更关心参与安排。自主试手关心自己的做法，生动表达关心呈现的色彩、声音或动作；这些都可以在安静环境发生。友善同玩强调商量怎样共同参与，可以包括并排各自画。不要把结果换算成内向程度，或宣称某两个标签罕见、紧张或天然互补。
paragraphs.en: Curious Explorer may be quiet while investigating real materials; Quiet Imaginer develops a fictional scene. Prepared Player may watch first but chiefly wants participation information. Independent Maker concerns a personal method and Expressive Player a form of presentation; either can happen quietly. Welcoming Companion can include drawing separately side by side by agreement. These results cannot convert into introversion or establish that any pair is rare, tense or naturally complementary.

title.en: Wanting company need not conflict

paragraphs.zh: 你可能喜欢一个人画小世界，又很想有人坐在旁边；也可能只在某些故事材料上愿意想象，其他时候更喜欢热闹游戏。两者都能真实存在。题目没有测量孤独、社交困难、专注能力或自我调节，更不能用低计数推断缺少想象力。若这一名称不合适，可直接留下“今天更想画小房间”这样的事实，不用把它升级成一辈子的性格结论。
paragraphs.en: You may want to draw a little world privately while wanting someone nearby, or enjoy imagining only with particular materials and prefer lively games elsewhere. Both can be true. These items assess no loneliness, social difficulty, attention capacity or self-regulation, and lower counts cannot establish a lack of imagination. If the name does not fit, retain a practical description such as wanting to draw a small room today rather than a lifelong personality conclusion.

title.zh: 给想象一个可停止的边界
title.en: An imagining space with an available ending

paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，在纸上画一个三分钟就能停下的小场景，不用解释它象征什么。你可以独自画、和自选同伴并排画，或不做。之后注意自己更喜欢构思、细节还是当时的安静条件即可。没有必须完成的作品和成长目标，也无需找童年记忆验证它。这个观察不具备治疗承诺，不能推断被忽略的经历；公开正文与私人想象始终可以分开。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, draw a little scene you can stop after three minutes without explaining what it symbolises. Work alone, beside a chosen companion or not at all. Afterwards, notice whether imagining, details or the quiet setting appealed. There is no required finished piece or growth target and no need for childhood memories to validate it. This observation offers no treatment and cannot reveal neglect; a public guide can remain separate from private imagination.

title.en: 18-item counts, ties and close results

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，对应标签加1，原始次数合计18。每题提供六种玩法中的四种；六类各出现12次，在四个位置各3次，未出现的两类不记为被拒绝。分母12是选项出现次数，不是你有多少童心、性格百分比或人群排名。所有最高计数保留完整说明；全选同一位置会六类各3，六份全部呈现，不把名单第一位当主型。差一次只是一项选择，不证明显著差异、稀有度或固定主副型，近分也不补造混合类型。计数是相对分布，一项多选必然挤掉当题其他选项，不是六项独立能力或心理特质的强度。换时间、材料、场地或同伴可能改变回答。

Every approach appears twelve times and three times in each position; absent approaches are not counted as rejected. Twelve is an exposure denominator, not an amount of childlike spirit, personality percentage or population rank. Every highest count retains its full guide. Choosing the same position throughout gives three each and displays all six without prioritising the first. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference, rarity or fixed primary and secondary type; close counts create no invented hybrid. Counts are relative: selecting an option displaces others in that question rather than measuring six independent abilities or psychological intensities. Time, materials, setting and company can change responses.

title.en: Scope of this original adult reflection

paragraphs.en: This independently authored FermatMind reflection is for adults and uses eighteen original present-day situations, seventy-two original options and six editorial reading labels. Background health material shows that the concept also appears in professional contexts without validating this mapping, algorithm or interpretation. No competitor ten-item bank, prose, persona or standard clinical instrument is adopted, and recalling harm or explaining family history is unnecessary. Results establish no trauma, parentification, neurotype, attachment, empathy, health, childhood cause or career. This is neither IFS, schema therapy, an egogram, a child assessment nor a therapy exercise. You may decline completion, sharing or exploration of the past, and can leave without finding personal evidence for the name.

title.zh: 友善同玩结果：内在童年测试完整说明
title.en: Welcoming Companion: Inner Child Test Full Result Guide

description.zh: 本次较常选邀请、轮流和共同决定的玩法。它关注自愿参与，不认证共情、照顾者身份、亲职化或人际能力。
description.en: Explore Welcoming Companion through invitations, turns and five comparisons. Full examples without caregiving duties, empathy or parentification verdicts.

title.zh: 同玩不等于照顾所有人
title.en: Playing together is not caring for everyone

paragraphs.zh: 友善同玩是想和愿意的人商量怎样玩：各做一页、轮流一句、留出可加入也可旁观的位置。它不要求你先察觉所有人的感受、承担活动成败或让每个人开心。结果只对应本题中共同参与的选项，没有测出共情、善良、情绪劳动或小时候照顾过谁。你可以不邀请、不回应一次邀约，也可以享受独处；这些都不会让你失去这份结果要求的资格，因为它没有设定资格。
paragraphs.en: Welcoming Companion concerns agreeing how to play with willing people: a page each, a line in turn or room to join or watch. It requires no detection of everyone’s feelings, responsibility for the activity or duty to make people happy. These options assess no empathy, goodness, emotional labour or whom you cared for in childhood. You can decline invitations or enjoy time alone without losing qualification for the result; no such qualification is defined.

title.en: Drawing together need not produce one picture

paragraphs.zh: 两个人想做趣味小册，你先问对方想画什么，再各选一页。对方想看不想画，你可以接受，自己的那页仍然成立。共同选择不一定让成果更好，也不需要证明你会协调关系。若今天只有你一个人，照样能玩；若对方改变主意，邀请也可以结束。这个例子描述参与安排，而不是从一次主动邀请推断你天生会照顾他人或童年承担了责任。
paragraphs.en: For a playful booklet, you might ask what the other person wants to draw and each choose a page. If they prefer watching, your own page can still happen. Shared choice does not guarantee a better result or prove relationship-coordination skill. You can play alone when nobody joins, and an invitation can end if someone changes their mind. This describes participation rather than inferring an inborn caregiving role or childhood responsibility from one invitation.

title.en: Making participation and refusal visible

paragraphs.zh: 共同活动常需要谈清材料、时间和可选择的角色。你可以邀请一次，说明可以拒绝，然后继续自己的安排；无需把沉默读成不开心，更不用负责猜原因。对方想独自做一部分时，仍可能喜欢与你一起待着。友善在这里是选项的名称，而非道德等级或评价他人的标准。现实中的照顾义务与关系承诺需要独立讨论，不由趣味结果增加。
paragraphs.en: Shared activities may require discussing materials, time and optional roles. Invite once, make refusal welcome and continue your own arrangement without reading silence as unhappiness or guessing its cause. Someone may enjoy your company while making a separate part. Welcoming is a label for options here rather than a moral rank or standard for judging others. Real care responsibilities and relationship commitments need their own discussion; a playful result adds none.

title.en: Asking something that may be declined

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“你想一起折两只船，还是各做各的？今天不想也可以”，不必说“我是照顾者，所以不能让你落单”。前一种表达提供具体选择，后一种却替别人决定了需要。你也可以提出自己只想做一小会儿，或今天不想协调。你的乐趣和时间同样可以写进约定；共同玩不是一份自动分配给你的工作，更不是证明值得被喜欢的任务。
paragraphs.en: You could offer folding boats together or making separate things, with declining equally welcome, instead of assuming a caregiver identity obliges you to prevent someone being alone. A concrete invitation provides choices; an identity claim decides needs for the other person. You may also say you want only a short activity or no coordination today. Include your time and enjoyment in the arrangement. Shared play is neither automatically assigned work nor a task for earning approval.

title.zh: 共同参与可以容纳五种玩法
title.en: Shared participation can hold five approaches

paragraphs.zh: 好奇发问可以邀请别人观察同一纹理，自主试手可以各做自己的版本，准备入场可以共同确认规则。生动表达不等于喜欢同玩，安静想象也不等于拒绝同伴；两种活动都能自愿共享。友善同玩主要关心怎样商量参与，而非必须选择相同内容。最高并列不用解释成照顾者与独立者冲突，也不能推断哪类搭档最适合你或谁应该补足谁。
paragraphs.en: Curious Explorer can invite someone to examine a texture; Independent Maker can involve separate personal versions; Prepared Player can discuss rules jointly. Expressive Player does not imply wanting company, and Quiet Imaginer does not imply rejecting it. Either can be shared voluntarily. Welcoming Companion chiefly concerns agreeing participation rather than choosing identical content. A tie establishes no caregiver-versus-independent conflict or evidence about ideal partners and who should complete whom.

title.en: Not inviting establishes no coldness

paragraphs.zh: 你可能只是这次看到的同玩选项很轻松，实际碰到时间紧或不熟悉的人时更想自己做。也可能本来喜欢陪伴，但题目给出的活动并不合口味。不同选择不能证明共情多少，更不能由计数反推被迫照顾大人、家庭角色或创伤。低计数也不表示自私、不合群或不值得被照顾。如果名称让你想到职责，可以不用它，直接描述哪一次邀请令你愉快。
paragraphs.en: Shared options may look relaxed here while limited time or unfamiliar company make independent play preferable. You might enjoy company but dislike the particular activities offered. Choices establish no amount of empathy and cannot retrospectively identify forced care for adults, family roles or trauma. Lower counts establish no selfishness, lack of sociability or unworthiness of care. If the name suggests duty, set it aside and describe a particular invitation you enjoyed instead.

title.en: One mutually optional invitation

paragraphs.zh: 若你愿意，给熟悉且愿意的人一个短活动邀请，同时说明两人都可改变主意。问清各自想做什么和什么时候结束，不必追问私人感受。也可以选择不给任何人发邀请。之后只回顾商量过程是否符合自己的意愿，不给关系打分。这不是练习当治疗师、修复家庭或提升共情的方法；没有疗愈承诺，也无须把答题结果或童年经历发给同伴。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, offer a brief activity to someone familiar and interested, making it clear either person can change their mind. Agree what each wants to do and when to finish without requesting private feelings. You may also send no invitation. Afterwards, consider whether the arrangement suited your wishes rather than rating the relationship. This is no exercise in becoming a therapist, repairing family life or improving empathy. It promises no healing and requires sharing neither test results nor childhood experiences.

title.en: How eighteen choices produce six counts

paragraphs.zh: 每道题提供六种玩法中的四种，选中一项就为对应方向加1，18题原始计数合计18。每种玩法各出现12次，并在四个选项位置各出现3次，单项次数范围0—12。某题未出现的两个方向没有被你比较，因此不能把它们记作被拒绝；也没有反向题、额外权重或随机抽取。
paragraphs.en: Each question offers four of the six approaches. Choosing one adds one count to its direction, for a total of eighteen. Each approach appears twelve times, three times in each option position, giving a possible individual range of 0–12. The two absent approaches were not compared and cannot be counted as rejected. There are no reverse keys, extra weights or random result selection.

paragraphs.zh: 例如，按目录顺序得到5、5、2、2、3、1，好奇发问与自主试手同为最高，便同时呈现两份完整结果。5/12表示在该方向出现的12次里选了5次，不是41.7%的性格、准确率或人群位置。计数总和固定，一项多选会挤掉当题其他选项，不能当作六种独立心理特质的强度。
paragraphs.en: For example, counts of 5, 5, 2, 2, 3, 1 in the listed order give Curious Explorer and Independent Maker the joint maximum, so both complete results appear. Five out of twelve means five selections across twelve opportunities, not 41.7% of a personality, accuracy or a population rank. With a fixed total, selecting one displaces others in that question; these are not six independent trait intensities.

title.zh: 最高并列、近分与未完成结果
title.en: Highest ties, close counts and incomplete attempts

paragraphs.zh: 所有同为最高的方向都保留，不按字母、题号、名单顺序或所谓主副型强分先后。一直选择同一位置时，六项会各得3次，六份结果全部呈现。这个例子说明并列是规则允许的结果，不是系统出错，也不能据此判断一个人“什么都会”或完全没有偏好。
paragraphs.en: Every direction sharing the maximum is retained, without alphabetic, question-order, list-order or primary/secondary priority. Choosing one option position throughout gives three counts to each and displays all six results. This is an allowed tie, not a system failure, proof of being good at everything or evidence of having no preferences.

paragraphs.zh: 最高5次、另一项4次时仍按原始次数显示，不自动改成并列，也不宣称一票差距具有统计意义。可以把近分的两份说明一起读，但它们不会生成第七种混合类型。未完成18题只保留进度，不提前给个人结论；公开指南可随时先读。
paragraphs.en: If the highest count is five and another is four, both retain their actual counts. They are not merged into a tie or treated as a statistically meaningful difference. You may read nearby guides together, but no seventh hybrid type is created. Before all eighteen choices, only progress is available, not a personal conclusion; public guides remain open.

title.zh: 内在小孩的概念与本站原创题本
title.en: The inner-child concept and this original questionnaire

paragraphs.zh: “内在小孩”在健康教育中可以指童年经验及其影响的一种表述。 本页采用更窄的娱乐用法：只比较成人现在愿意选择的低风险玩法。18道情境、72个选项和六个阅读标签均由费马原创，不是六种已获临床承认的儿童人格，也不把标签对应为某段年龄或家庭角色。
paragraphs.en: Health education uses inner child as a way to describe childhood experiences and their influence. This page takes a narrower entertainment use: comparing low-stakes play an adult would choose now. Its eighteen situations, seventy-two options and six reading labels are original FermatMind content, not six clinically recognized child personalities, age periods or family roles.

paragraphs.zh: 因此，喜欢先看示范，只能在本题组里支持“准备入场”这一读法，不能倒推出童年缺乏安全感；喜欢同玩，也不能倒推出小时候照顾大人。请先核对问题实际问了什么，再判断结果能说明什么。专业概念的名称、背景资料或详细报告，都不能单独验证这份原创题本。[1]
paragraphs.en: Preferring a demonstration can support a Prepared Player reading within this set; it cannot establish childhood insecurity. Enjoying shared play cannot establish caring for adults as a child. Check what the questions actually ask before deciding what a result supports. Professional terminology, background sources and detailed reports do not by themselves validate this original form.[1]

title.zh: 好奇发问与自主试手：理解材料，还是试出版本
title.en: Curious Explorer and Independent Maker: understanding or making

paragraphs.zh: 好奇发问侧重观察差异、追问原因：同一张纸折成不同形状，为什么站立方式不一样？自主试手侧重自己调整做法：不急着得到解释，先改一下折痕试出另一个版本。两者可以同在一次活动里，但前者的兴趣落在问题与线索，后者落在操作与改动。
paragraphs.en: Curious Explorer emphasizes noticing differences and asking why: why do folds in the same paper stand differently? Independent Maker emphasizes adjusting a method: before needing an explanation, change a crease and try another version. Both can occur in one activity, but one foregrounds questions and clues, the other manipulation and revision.

paragraphs.zh: 这里比较的是更想先做哪一步，不是科学能力、手工熟练度或胆量。第一次接触材料时，有人很想试手却做得不熟；熟悉技术的人也可能更想研究一个小问题。可以说“我先看看它为什么这样”，或“我想自己试个版本”；这些话表达参与偏好，不是要求别人配合的理由。
paragraphs.en: The comparison concerns what you want to do first, not scientific ability, craft skill or bravery. A beginner may want to build without being skilled; an experienced maker may prefer investigating a small question. “I want to see why it works” and “I would like to try my version” state preferences, not reasons others must accommodate them.

title.zh: 准备入场与生动表达：安排条件，还是呈现点子
title.en: Prepared Player and Expressive Player: conditions or expression

paragraphs.zh: 准备入场侧重先知道材料、规则和参与步骤，再选择怎样加入。生动表达侧重颜色、动作、台词或造型带来的鲜明呈现。以纸偶小舞台为例，先看怎样固定纸偶，与给角色编一句夸张台词，是不同的兴趣入口，并不彼此排斥。
paragraphs.en: Prepared Player emphasizes understanding materials, rules and participation steps before joining. Expressive Player emphasizes vivid presentation through color, movement, lines or shapes. At a paper-puppet stage, checking how a puppet is mounted and inventing an exaggerated line are different entry points, without excluding one another.

paragraphs.zh: 先问规则不等于焦虑或风险识别能力高；喜欢夸张表达不等于情绪失控、外向或需要观众赞赏。若你今天只想安静地做鲜明图案，也可以符合生动表达的部分内容。用一次具体选择和一次不适用的反例核对，比把标签当成永远的性格更清楚。
paragraphs.en: Asking about rules does not establish anxiety or superior risk judgment. Enjoying exaggerated expression does not establish emotional dysregulation, extraversion or a need for applause. Quietly making a vivid pattern may still fit an expressive preference. Compare a fitting choice with a counterexample rather than treating the label as a permanent personality.

title.zh: 安静想象与友善同玩：私下构思，还是共同展开
title.en: Quiet Imaginer and Welcoming Companion: private or shared play

paragraphs.zh: 安静想象侧重慢慢构思角色、细节与小世界，活动可以不需要观众。友善同玩侧重邀请愿意的人、轮流与一起决定，让玩法在互动中展开。同样是设计纸上小镇，一个人画房间的故事，与和伙伴各画一条街，都可能让人投入。
paragraphs.en: Quiet Imaginer emphasizes taking time with characters, details and little worlds, without needing an audience. Welcoming Companion emphasizes invitations, turns and shared decisions that let play unfold through interaction. In a paper town, inventing a room’s story alone and drawing separate streets with a partner can both be absorbing.

paragraphs.zh: 选择安静不证明孤独、社交困难或内向；选择同玩不证明共情能力，也不意味着要负责让所有人开心。邀请需要对方愿意，拒绝加入也应被尊重。可以说明“我想先自己画一会儿”，或“你想一起加一个小地方吗？”；两种方式都保留各自的选择空间。
paragraphs.en: Choosing quiet play does not establish loneliness, social difficulty or introversion. Choosing company does not certify empathy or a duty to keep everyone happy. An invitation depends on willingness, and declining it deserves respect. “I would like to draw alone first” and “Would you like to add a little place?” both leave room for choice.

title.zh: 一张废纸的六种玩法：把解释变成可观察的选择
title.en: Six approaches to scrap paper: making the reading observable

paragraphs.zh: 如果手边已有一张可用废纸，可以自愿选一种玩法：观察不同折痕的效果；自行搭一个支架；先看一个简单示范；做夸张的图案或角色；画一个不必展示的小场景；邀请愿意的人各添一部分。不需要购买材料、邀请儿童、录制作品或完成某个标准。
paragraphs.en: If scrap paper is already available, optionally choose one approach: observe different creases, build a support your own way, watch a simple demonstration, make a vivid pattern or character, draw a private little scene, or invite a willing person to add a part. No purchase, child participation, recording or performance standard is needed.

paragraphs.zh: 这不是第19道计分题，也不是治疗或提高分数的训练。可以记下你实际先做什么、过程中改了什么、是否想继续；没有兴趣也可结束。活动选择和测试标签不一致时，保留这个反例，不必为了符合报告而改变玩法。
paragraphs.en: This is no nineteenth scored item, therapy exercise or training to improve a score. You may note what you did first, changed along the way and wanted to continue; stop if it does not appeal. If your activity differs from the label, keep that counterexample rather than changing how you play to fit the report.

title.zh: 成人玩心研究与六种编辑标签有什么不同
title.en: Adult playfulness research versus six editorial labels

paragraphs.zh: 成人玩心已有专门研究，例如OLIW模型区分面向他人、轻松随兴、智性和奇趣四个侧面；研究综述也指出定义与结构仍有多种方案。[2] 这不等于六种内在儿童的分类。本页没有施测OLIW条目，也不能把六项次数换成它的分数。
paragraphs.en: Adult playfulness has dedicated research: the OLIW model distinguishes Other-directed, Lighthearted, Intellectual and Whimsical facets, while a review notes differing definitions and structures.[2] This is not a taxonomy of six inner children. This page does not administer OLIW items or convert six counts into its scores.

paragraphs.zh: 日常语言相似不代表测量相同。“想自己做”“喜欢共同玩”在这里是选项含义，不是已经验证的独立特质。本站尚未建立该题本的信度、效度、跨语言等价与常模；计分可复算说明规则透明，不说明结果能揭示潜意识、童年成因或预测生活表现。
paragraphs.en: Similar everyday language does not establish equivalent measurement. Wanting to make something yourself or share play describes choices here, not validated independent traits. Reliability, validity, language equivalence and norms are not established for this form. Reproducible scoring makes its rules transparent without revealing a subconscious, childhood causes or future performance.

title.zh: 偏好会受条件影响，重测怎样理解
title.en: Context-sensitive preferences and interpreting a retake

paragraphs.zh: 同一人面对熟悉材料、陌生规则、充足时间或嘈杂场地，可能选择不同方式。一次想先看示范，另一次想直接动手，可以反映任务与条件变化。问自己“现在什么更吸引我”，比试图猜测一个永恒不变的童年标签更符合本页题意。
paragraphs.en: Familiar materials, unfamiliar rules, available time or a noisy setting may change a person’s choices. Watching a demonstration once and building immediately another time can reflect different tasks and conditions. Asking what appeals now fits these questions better than guessing an unchanging childhood identity.

paragraphs.zh: 若重测计数改变，先比较哪些题变了、当时环境和同伴是否相同。一票变化可能改变最高方向，但没有可靠改变阈值，不能据此认定成熟、退步、疗愈或创伤消失。你可以记录有用的活动条件，也可以只把结果当作一次轻松阅读。
paragraphs.en: If counts change on a retake, compare the changed items, setting and company first. One changed choice may alter the leading direction, but no reliable-change threshold establishes maturity, deterioration, healing or resolved trauma. You may record useful activity conditions or simply enjoy the result as a light reading.

title.zh: 适用对象、回忆选择与结果使用
title.en: Audience, freedom from recall and appropriate use

paragraphs.zh: 本页为成人的当下娱乐探索设计，不用于评估儿童发展、家庭关系、心理健康、依恋、亲职化或职业。题目只涉及普通低风险玩法，不要求回忆、描述或想象受伤经历，也没有隐藏的家庭评判题。若你想了解过去的真实事件，本页选择不能提供事实证据。
paragraphs.en: This is present-day entertainment reflection for adults, not assessment of child development, family relationships, mental health, attachment, parentification or careers. Items concern ordinary low-stakes play, without recalling, describing or imagining hurtful experiences or hidden questions judging family members. These choices cannot supply factual evidence about past events.

paragraphs.zh: 可以不完成、不分享、不探究过去，也不用为结果寻找符合的记忆。退出不被解释成回避或压抑。指南中的表达和活动只是可选建议，不要求和解、邀请某个人参与或接受别人给你的标签；其他测评仍需独立完整作答。
paragraphs.en: You may decline completion, sharing and exploring the past without searching for matching memories. Leaving is not interpreted as avoidance or repression. Guide wording and activities are optional, with no requirement to reconcile, involve a particular person or accept someone else’s label. Other assessments still require their own complete responses.

title.zh: 免费完整结果、直接开始与隐私
title.en: Free complete results, direct start and privacy

paragraphs.zh: 完整18题、全部原始次数、所有最高并列与六份完整公开指南均免费，无需注册、邮箱或前置测评。约6分钟是阅读与思考的估计，不是计时限制；开始按钮直接进入第一题，没有再次同意或付费解锁步骤。
paragraphs.en: All eighteen items, raw counts, every highest tie and six full public guides are free, without signup, email or a prerequisite test. About six minutes estimates reading and reflection, not a time limit. Start opens the first question directly without another agreement or payment to unlock results.

paragraphs.zh: 答案在浏览器内计分，不随计分请求上传，也不写入网址或分析事件。只有主动保存才会在本标签页保留最多24小时的草稿，完成、重测或退出清除即删除。可选分享包含公开标签与指南链接，不含私人答案、次数或故事；其他不含答案的使用事件依隐私与Cookie设置。
paragraphs.en: Answers are scored in your browser, without a scoring upload or answer-bearing URLs or analytics events. Only opted-in drafts remain in this tab for up to 24 hours, clearing on completion, retake or exit-and-clear. Optional sharing includes public labels and guide links, not private answers, counts or stories; other usage events without answers follow privacy and cookie settings.

question.zh: 内在童年性格测试到底测什么？
question.en: What does this Inner Child Personality Test actually explore?

answer.zh: 本页比较你现在愿意选择的六种玩法，是给成人的原创娱乐反思。不还原小时候的性格，不评创伤、儿童发展或真实家庭经历。
answer.en: It compares six approaches to play you would choose now, as an original adult entertainment reflection. It reconstructs no childhood personality and assesses no trauma, child development or actual family history.

answer.zh: 好奇发问、自主试手、准备入场、生动表达、安静想象和友善同玩。它们分别关注问题、改动、条件、呈现、构思和共同参与，可以在同一活动里出现。
answer.en: Curious Explorer, Independent Maker, Prepared Player, Expressive Player, Quiet Imaginer and Welcoming Companion emphasize questions, revision, conditions, presentation, imagination and shared participation. They can occur in the same activity.

question.zh: 这些是学术公认的六种内在儿童吗？
question.en: Are these six academically established inner-child types?

answer.zh: 不是。它们是本站编辑阅读标签。专业概念或成人玩心研究不验证本页六分类，也不把它们对应为年龄、家庭角色或治疗阶段。
answer.en: No. They are this website’s editorial reading labels. Professional concepts and adult playfulness research do not validate this six-way classification or map it to ages, family roles or therapy stages.

question.zh: 需要想起童年或受伤经历吗？
question.en: Do I need to recall childhood or painful experiences?

answer.zh: 不需要。按当下更想尝试的普通活动作答，不要求描述家庭、重演伤害或寻找被遗忘的记忆。可以不完成或退出。
answer.en: No. Answer for ordinary activities you would like to try now. There is no family account, reenactment of harm or search for forgotten memories. You may leave or decline completion.

question.zh: 每题怎么选，多个都喜欢怎么办？
question.en: How do I choose if several options appeal?

answer.zh: 选目前更想先做的一项；都不特别喜欢时，选相对愿意尝试的。不按童年的自己、理想身份或看起来更好的标签作答。
answer.en: Choose what you would do first now; if none especially appeals, pick what you are relatively willing to try. Do not answer for your childhood self, an ideal identity or a supposedly better label.

question.zh: 18题怎样计分，12这个分母是什么？
question.en: How are eighteen choices scored, and what does twelve mean?

answer.zh: 每选一项，对应方向加1，合计18。六方向各出现12次，次数0—12；12是出现机会，不是相似度、人群排名或童心百分比。
answer.en: Each choice adds one to its direction, for a total of eighteen. Each direction appears twelve times, giving counts from 0–12. Twelve represents opportunities, not similarity, population rank or a childlike percentage.

question.zh: 为什么会有两个或六个结果？
question.en: Why might I receive two or six results?

answer.zh: 所有最高计数均保留。5、5、2、2、3、1有两项最高；一直选同一位置会六项各3，六份都显示。并列不会随机只取一个。
answer.en: Every maximum is retained. Counts of 5,5,2,2,3,1 have two maxima; choosing the same position throughout gives three each and displays all six. Ties are not reduced to a randomly selected result.

question.zh: 差一次能说明哪个更像我吗？
question.en: Does one additional choice establish which fits me better?

answer.zh: 它只说明本次多选一次，不证明显著差异或固定主次型。近分可以一起阅读，但本页不强行合并计数或新增混合类型。
answer.en: It records one extra choice in this attempt, not a significant difference or fixed primary/secondary type. Read close guides together if useful; no counts are merged and no hybrid identity is added.

question.zh: 选择准备入场代表焦虑吗？

answer.zh: 不代表。它表示在这些情境里较常选择先看示范、了解安排，不测情绪症状、风险识别能力或童年原因。
answer.en: No. It records more choices to see demonstrations and understand arrangements in these situations, not emotional symptoms, risk-detection ability or childhood causes.

question.zh: 安静想象与友善同玩能判断内外向、共情吗？
question.en: Can Quiet Imaginer or Welcoming Companion establish introversion or empathy?

answer.zh: 不能。私下构思与共同参与是活动偏好，不能换算内外向或共情，也不说明孤独、照顾者身份或亲职化。
answer.en: No. Private imagining and shared participation are activity preferences. They do not convert into introversion or empathy or establish loneliness, caregiving identity or parentification.

question.zh: 这和OLIW、IFS或模式疗法一样吗？
question.en: Is this OLIW, IFS or schema therapy?

answer.zh: 不同。本页没有施测OLIW，也不是心理治疗、自我状态图或儿童评估。六个编辑标签不能换算其他模型结果。
answer.en: No. It does not administer OLIW and is not psychotherapy, an egogram or child assessment. Six editorial labels cannot be converted into another model’s results.

question.zh: 怎么把结果用于日常而不贴标签？
question.en: How can I use the result without labeling myself?

answer.zh: 选一个自愿小活动，观察自己先做什么，再找一次不符合报告的反例。可尝试说明参与方式，不需模仿标签或追求某项更高。
answer.en: Choose an optional activity, observe what you do first and find a counterexample to the report. State how you would like to join without imitating a label or trying to raise a count.

question.zh: 重测变了是不是成长或疗愈？
question.en: Does a different retest mean growth or healing?

answer.zh: 不能据此判断。材料、时间、规则和同伴都可能改变选择。本站没有可靠改变阈值，也不测成熟度或治疗效果。
answer.en: Not from this alone. Materials, time, rules and company may change choices. No reliable-change threshold, maturity score or treatment outcome is measured.

question.zh: 是否免费，开始后要同意或保存答案吗？
question.en: Is it free, with an agreement or saved answers after Start?

answer.zh: 题目、计数、并列与六份全文全部免费，开始直接进入题目。保存需主动选择，答案仅浏览器计分；可选分享不含私人答案或次数。
answer.en: All items, counts, ties and six full guides are free, and Start opens questions directly. Saving is opt-in and scoring stays in the browser; optional sharing contains no private answers or counts.
